name: Mandarin Chinese
about: Each character is one syllable with its own meaning. Pinyin with tone marks shows the sound.

phrases.how: Characters carry meaning, not single sounds: 你 'you' + 好 'good'.
phrases.why: Greet someone in their own script on a card or a note.
phrases.dictation: Two characters. 你 has the 'person' part 亻 on the left; 好 is 女 then 子.

phrases.how: One character is one syllable; saying 谢 twice is the everyday 'thanks'.
phrases.why: Write a real thank-you card to a host or to family.
phrases.dictation: The same character twice. 谢 starts with the 'speech' part 讠 on the left.

phrases.how: 水 began as a picture of flowing water; many water words contain a form of it (氵).
phrases.why: Spot it on a menu, a sign or a bottle label.
phrases.dictation: One character, four strokes: the hooked middle line comes first.

phrases.how: Two characters, two syllables: 朋 and 友 both carry the idea of 'friend'.
phrases.why: Sign a note to a friend. Writing it by hand helps you remember it.
phrases.dictation: 朋 is two 月 side by side; 友 starts with a short horizontal line.

phrases.how: Numbers are characters too: 一 is one stroke, 二 is two, 三 is three.
phrases.why: Read quantities and order one of something off a menu.
phrases.dictation: One horizontal stroke, left to right.
